rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something is available without payment.

example.english: This exhibition is free to enter.
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 zin2 laam5 min5 fai3 jap6 coeng4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when letting a person or animal go free.

example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 fong3 zau2 zek3 gau2 laa1

rows.note: Use this when releasing a particular person, especially someone detained or being held.

example.english: The police finally decided to free him.
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 zeoi3 hau6 kyut3 ding6 fong3 jan4

rows.note: Use this formal term in legal, official, or written contexts for releasing someone from custody or captivity.

example.english: The court ordered the defendant to be set free.
example.jyutping: faat3 ting4 haa6 ling6 sik1 fong3 bei6 gou3

rows.note: This is the default choice for something obtainable without payment.

example.english: Entry to this exhibition is free.
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 zin2 laam5 min5 fai3 jap6 coeng4 gaa3

rows.note: Use this for being unconstrained or politically and personally free, including not being imprisoned.

example.english: After getting out of prison, I’m finally free.
example.traditional: 出獄之後，我終於自由喇。
example.jyutping: ceot1 juk6 zi1 hau6 ngo5 zung1 jyu1 zi6 jau4 laa3

rows.note: Use this when someone has no commitments and is available or has free time.

example.english: Call me when you are free.
example.jyutping: nei5 dak1 haan4 sin1 daa2 bei2 ngo5 laa1

rows.note: Use this construction when something is without or does not contain the specified N.

example.english: This coffee is free of sugar.
example.jyutping: nei1 bui1 gaa3 fe1 mou5 tong4
